title: The evening examen
tomorrow: what were Jesus's last words in Luke, and where did he get them?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the family table: bread broken at Emmaus, and a hadith that puts the blessing in eating together. The line was a small communion.

Lights off, phone on the charger, and the day starts replaying on its own: the thing you said, the message you sent too fast, the face someone made. The replay usually asks one question, what went wrong. Saint Ignatius of Loyola taught a short evening practice that asks a better one first. It's called the examen, and it doesn't start with blame. It starts with thanks.
screen: `THE NIGHTLY REPLAY.` → `WHAT WENT WRONG?` → `IT STARTS WITH THANKS.`

segments.voice: In the Spiritual Exercises, Ignatius lays it out in a few plain steps. Give thanks to God for the gifts of the day. Ask for light to see it truly. Go back through the day hour by hour, from the moment you woke. Ask pardon where it's needed. Then resolve, with God's help, to do better tomorrow. Notice the order. Thanks comes before faults, and light comes before the looking. It echoes a much older evening review. At the end of the sixth day in Genesis, in the Douay-Rheims: "God saw all the things that he had made, and they were very good." So try it on this week. A road walked with eyes up. A first task offered. A minute at noon. A slump you stayed through. A blessing at the door. A table faced together. Where was God in any of it? Some of those went well and some didn't. The examen holds both, and it starts with the good.
screen: `THANKS, THEN LIGHT.` · `HOUR BY HOUR, FROM WAKING.` · `PARDON, THEN TOMORROW.` · `GOD SAW, AND IT WAS VERY GOOD.` · then, large: `WHERE WAS GOD?`

segments.voice: Go back through today from the moment you woke, slowly, like scrolling a camera roll. Stop at one moment you're grateful for and one you'd take back. Ask quietly, of each, where God was in it.
The evening examen. Ignatius's short look back over the day: thanks first, then light, then pardon, then tomorrow.
Your line: where was God, asked once before sleep. A good week, and it's done.

screen: `DAY 1631 COUNTS.` → `ORDINARY HOLINESS · 11 OF 80.` → `TOMORROW: WHAT WERE JESUS'S LAST WORDS IN LUKE, AND WHERE DID HE GET THEM?`

howItsDone: Jesuits and many other Catholics pray the examen each evening, and some also at midday; a short examination of conscience is part of Night Prayer.

notes: Spiritual Exercises 43 paraphrased: thanks for benefits received; grace to know sins; an account of the soul from rising, hour by hour; pardon; a resolve to amend with God's grace. The trapdoor's 'five points' is stated in the text itself ('It contains in it five Points'); confirm.
Douay-Rheims Genesis 1:31 quoted from memory; confirm exact Challoner wording.
'Where was God' is the outline's carry, a modern summary of the examen's spirit, not Ignatius's own wording; the script does not attribute it to him.
